research_question: Research verified literature where user next-item behavior, hyperbolic geometry and generative semantic IDs intersect.

sources.title: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval

verified_overlap.user_next_item_behavior: Direct: the abstract states that a Transformer sequence-to-sequence model predicts the Semantic ID of the next item a user will interact with, given Semantic IDs in the user's session.
verified_overlap.generative_semantic_ids: Direct: items receive semantically meaningful tuples of codewords serving as Semantic IDs, which the retrieval model autoregressively decodes.
verified_overlap.hyperbolic_geometry: No evidence located in the inspected arXiv record/full-text-linked material; do not treat this paper as hyperbolic evidence.

sources.scope_note: Strong verified evidence for the behavior + generative semantic-ID pair, not the three-way intersection.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Predict the next item from the ordered item interactions in a user's session, using semantic IDs as the autoregressively generated target.
behavior_problem_candidates.status: Established behavior task in the cited work; hyperbolic modeling is not established by this source.

behavior_problem_candidates.candidate: Test whether hyperbolic representations of user/session behavior improve next-item prediction while retaining generative semantic-ID decoding.
behavior_problem_candidates.status: Research hypothesis only. No independently verified full-text source demonstrating this combined design was found in this bounded search.

limitations: The verified source directly supports next-item prediction and generative Semantic IDs, but does not establish hyperbolic geometry; therefore it must not be cited as evidence for the full intersection.
No independently verified source establishing all three elements together is included. The absence of such a source in this search is not proof that none exists.
FULL_TEXT is used only for the arXiv-hosted full text that is directly linked from the verified record. No claim about unseen future/test interactions is made.
The hyperbolic next-item + generative semantic-ID combination is presented solely as an UNKNOWN research candidate, not as a result reported in prior literature.
